title: Dual-battery setups evaluate low/critical battery thresholds against raw percentage sum (up to 200%) rather than capacity-weighted average
line: With two batteries, low and critical battery warnings now use the real combined charge instead of the two percentages added together.
explanation: Powerdevil's Core::currentChargePercent() added up the percentages of all system batteries, so two batteries at 30% and 20% counted as 50%. Low/critical warnings, the LowBattery profile and the critical action were all judged against that sum: warnings fired with a wrong percentage, and with default thresholds they came far too late (two batteries at 8% and 6% never warned). Open MR !692 computes the combined charge as total energy over total full energy of the present batteries (one battery keeps its own percentage; the mean is the fallback without energy data), re-checks thresholds when batteries appear or disappear and when AC is unplugged, and adds autotests.

commits.message: Calculate system battery charge from available energy (MR !692, 5 commits by Vibhor Goel, applied unchanged)

media.caption: Reporter's case on master: Low battery level 50%, batteries at 30% and 20% (100 Wh each, real charge 25%): the warning says 50% Remaining
Same steps with MR !692: the warning says 25% Remaining
Default thresholds (low 10%) on master, batteries dropped from 40%/40% to 8%/6% (real 7%): no warning, profile stays Battery
Same steps with MR !692: Battery Low (7% Remaining), profile switches to LowBattery

review.text: Applies the open MR !692 unchanged; it fixes the real cause (Core::currentChargePercent() summing percentages) by weighting by energy, with sensible fallbacks and unit tests, and the rig shows the wrong 50% warning becoming 25% and the missing 8%/6% warning now firing. It is larger than this bug needs (commits 3-5 are separable extras), but that is the MR author's call and should be settled in the MR review, not by a competing fix.
